introduction: At this foundational level, we cover the two most fundamental principles of surveying, linear measurements, and map scales. These concepts form the absolute baseline for all preliminary exams.

core_concepts.title: Fundamental Principles of Surveying
core_concepts.description:
1. **To work from Whole to Part:** The area is first enclosed by major control points, and then minor details are measured. This prevents the accumulation of errors and localizes them.
2. **To locate a new point by at least two measurements:** Any new point must be established using at least two independent measurements (linear or angular) from reference points.

core_concepts.title: Chain Surveying
core_concepts.description:
1. **Principle:** Triangulation. The entire area is divided into a network of well-conditioned triangles.
2. **Well-Conditioned Triangle:** A triangle where no angle is less than $30^{\circ}$ or greater than $120^{\circ}$. Ideally, an equilateral triangle is the best.
3. **Metric Chain:** Typically available in 20 meters (100 links) or 30 meters (150 links). The length of a single link is exactly 20 cm.

core_concepts.title: Representative Fraction (R.F.)
core_concepts.description:
It is the ratio of the map distance to the corresponding actual distance on the ground. 
**$\text{R.F.} = \frac{\text{Distance on Map}}{\text{Actual Ground Distance}}$** 
Note: Both values must be in the same unit. The larger the scale, the higher the R.F. value (e.g., a 1:100 scale is larger than a 1:10000 scale).

important_entities.name: Invar Tape
important_entities.significance: It is an alloy made of Nickel (36%) and Steel (64%). Because its coefficient of thermal expansion is extremely low, it is used for highly precise linear measurements, such as measuring a Base Line.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Whole to Part vs. Part to Whole
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: Examiners often try to confuse you with 'Part to Whole'. Remember, if we work from 'part to whole', small errors will expand and accumulate, ruining the survey network. The correct answer is ALWAYS **Work from Whole to Part**.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Invar is precisely 36% Nickel. The remainder (64%) is steel.

exam_strategy_tips: The most basic SSC JE question: 'What is the primary fundamental principle of surveying?' Answer: To work from whole to part.
